Notebook introduction

This document provides an exhaustive, bit-by-bit technical breakdown of the **FrameGraph (Render Graph) Subsystem** in the Retiam WebGPU Engine. It covers DAG compilation, dead-code culling, transient resource memory pooling, decorator-driven dependency tracking, modular render features (`IPlugin`), and step-by-step guides for creating custom passes and post-processing plugins.
1. Architectural Overview & Design Motivation
In traditional rendering engines, the render loop executes a rigid, hardcoded sequence of passes. This creates major architectural problems:

items: **VRAM Bloat**: Render targets (shadow maps, G-Buffers, post-process ping-pongs) remain permanently allocated in VRAM even when their lifespan is only a fraction of a frame.
**Pipeline Rigidity**: Adding custom effects (e.g. cel-shading outlines, bloom, raytracing, order-independent transparency) requires modifying monolithic render loop code.
**Lack of Dead-Code Culling**: Inactive passes continue to execute and consume GPU cycles.

blocks.text: The Retiam FrameGraph Solution:
Retiam utilizes an **Acyclic Directed Graph (DAG) Execution Model**:

items: **Virtual Resource Declarations**: Passes declare what resources they `@create`, `@read`, and `@write` using abstract handles (`TextureHandle`, `BufferHandle`).
**Automated Dependency Graph & Topological Sorting**: The engine analyzes inputs and outputs to determine the execution order using Kahn's algorithm.

**Dead-Code Elimination (Culling)**: Any pass whose outputs are not transitively consumed by an unculled sink (such as the canvas presentation pass) is automatically culled from the execution schedule.

**Transient Resource Aliasing & Memory Pooling**: Textures and buffers with non-overlapping execution lifetimes share the same underlying physical GPU allocations, reducing VRAM consumption by up to **70%**.

Textures and buffers define sizing rules dynamically:

items: **`relative`**: Dynamically scaled relative to canvas resolution (e.g. `scale: 1.0` for full resolution, `scale: 0.5` for half-res bloom).
**`custom`**: Sized via a custom callback function `(canvasWidth, canvasHeight) => { width, height }`.

blocks.text: 3. FrameGraph Compilation Lifecycle: Step-by-Step
When `frameGraph.compile()` is called, the graph executes a 5-phase optimization sequence:
Phase 1: Setup Phase & Version Tracking
The compiler iterates through all passes, executing `pass.onSetup(builder)`:

items: Decorator properties (`@read`, `@write`, `@create`) are parsed and added to internal tracking arrays.
In-place writes (`@write`) are versioned by aliasing the root resource with a new handle index.

blocks.text: Phase 2: Dead-Code Elimination (Culling)
The compiler traverses backwards from all **terminal sinks** (`isUnculled = true`, such as `PresentPass`):
Any pass that produces textures never read by an active downstream pass is automatically culled!
Phase 3: Topological Sorting (Kahn's Algorithm)
Dependencies are converted into directed edges ($A \to B$ where $B$ reads from $A$). The graph executes a topological sort to guarantee that producer passes always execute before consumer passes.
Phase 4: Resource Lifetime Analysis
For every active resource, the compiler records the index of the first pass that accesses it (`firstPassIndex`) and the last pass that consumes it (`lastPassIndex`).
Phase 5: Transient Resource Aliasing & Memory Pooling
When acquiring physical textures from [`ResourcePool.ts`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/render/frame_graph/ResourcePool.ts), the engine computes a hardware hash:
If an existing physical GPU texture with a matching hash has a lifespan that has **already ended** before the current pass starts, the physical texture is reused!

7. Best Practices & Troubleshooting

children: When reading depth textures in a post-process fragment shader, WebGPU requires creating a texture view with `{ aspect: 'depth-only' }` instead of binding a combined depth-stencil texture view.

If your custom pass writes to an offscreen target or drives external output, make sure to call `builder.markUnculled()` during `setup()`, or ensure its output is consumed by a downstream unculled pass.
When pipelines, canvas sizes, or shader parameters change, set `this.isDirty = true` on your pass to recreate bind groups and pipeline layouts.
If you add or remove features at runtime (e.g. toggling raytracing or bloom on keypress), set `renderer.frameGraphDirty = true` to trigger automatic DAG recompilation on the next frame.
